claims.claim: Frequent daytime napping was associated with a 48% higher dementia risk in 995 older U.S. Medicare beneficiaries followed for up to 10 years.
claims.episode_span: People who napped most days or every day had a 48% higher dementia risk
claims.source_title: Frequent Daytime Napping Linked to Higher Dementia Risk in Older Adults
claims.supporting_quote: The researchers found that participants who napped frequently—defined as most days or every day—had a 48% higher risk of developing dementia compared to those who rarely or never napped

claims.claim: Unintentional napping was associated with a 39% higher dementia risk, and naps of 30 minutes or less with a 40% higher risk.
claims.episode_span: Unintentional napping, falling asleep without meaning to, was linked to a 39% higher risk.
claims.source_title: Frequent Daytime Napping Linked to Higher Dementia Risk in Older Adults
claims.supporting_quote: Unintentional napping—defined as falling asleep without meaning to rather than planning a nap—was associated with a 39% higher risk of dementia. Napping for 30 minutes or less was also linked to a 40% higher risk

claims.claim: Adam Spira said more frequent napping could be a marker of brain changes rather than a cause.
claims.episode_span: Senior author Adam Spira said more frequent napping could be a marker of brain changes rather than a cause of them.
claims.source_title: Frequent Daytime Napping Linked to Higher Dementia Risk in Older Adults
claims.supporting_quote: More frequent napping could be a marker of changes in the brain, rather than a cause of brain changes that lead to dementia

claims.claim: A small human study reported in Aging Cell on September 27, 2026, found autophagy can increase, decrease, or remain unchanged with age depending on cell type and sex.
claims.episode_span: Activity could increase, decrease, or stay the same depending on cell type and sex.
claims.source_title: Scientists discover a surprising paradox in how our cells age
claims.supporting_quote: Instead, its activity can increase, decrease, or remain unchanged depending on the type of cell and a person's sex.

claims.claim: Caroline Kumsta said human evidence that autophagy declines with age is very thin.
claims.episode_span: the human evidence is very thin
claims.source_title: Scientists discover a surprising paradox in how our cells age
claims.supporting_quote: We commonly see people cite this idea that autophagy declines with age, but the actual evidence for this in humans is very thin

claims.claim: In a controlled comparison, 39% of GLP-1 users reported nail detachment versus 9% of never-users.
claims.episode_span: Nail detachment was reported by 39% of users and 9% of never-users
claims.source_title: Popular weight loss drugs linked to a surprising fingernail problem
claims.supporting_quote: Researchers found that 39% of GLP-1 users experienced nail detachment, compared with just 9% of people who had never taken the medications.

claims.claim: The nail comparison included 575 GLP-1 users and 1,329 never-users from France, the United States, Brazil, and Mexico.
claims.episode_span: Researchers compared 575 people using GLP-1 medications with 1,329 people
claims.source_title: Popular weight loss drugs linked to a surprising fingernail problem
claims.supporting_quote: researchers examined 575 people using GLP-1 medications and compared them with 1,329 individuals who had type 2 diabetes and/or obesity but had never used the drugs. Participants were recruited from France, the United States, Brazil, and Mexico.

claims.claim: A Nature Aging postmortem study identified 107 brain DNA methylation sites linked to Alzheimer’s pathology, with 38 replicated, and methylation partially mediated the APOE association with diagnosis.
claims.episode_span: It identified 107 brain DNA methylation sites linked to Alzheimer’s pathology, and 38 of those sites were replicated independently.
claims.source_title: Brain DNA methylation, APOE genotype and Alzheimer’s disease neuropathology in a large postmortem cohort
claims.supporting_quote: A large-scale study identified 107 brain DNA methylation sites linked to Alzheimer’s pathology, with 38 replicated independently. DNA methylation partially mediated the association between APOE genotype and Alzheimer’s diagnosis.

claims.claim: Antisense inhibition of miR-128-3p restored muscle mass and function in aged mice and improved muscle pathology in mouse and pig Duchenne models.
claims.episode_span: Antisense-oligonucleotide inhibition of miR-128-3p restored muscle mass and function in aged mice
claims.source_title: miR-128-3p Inhibition Improves Muscle Mass and Function in Aged Mice
claims.supporting_quote: antisense oligonucleotide -mediated inhibition of miR-128-3p restores muscle mass and function in aged mice, improves cardiac function while limiting adverse remodeling following myocardial infarction , and ameliorates skeletal and cardiac muscle pathology in mouse and pig models of Duchenne muscular dystrophy

claims.claim: The Sleep Heart Health Study of 5,407 adults found older age associated with shorter sleep, lower efficiency, and more arousals, not explained by chronic conditions including sleep apnea.
claims.episode_span: 5,407 community-dwelling adults, mean age 63 and ranging from 45 to 99, with 52% women, showed poorer objectively measured sleep with older age
claims.source_title: Subjective and objective sleep quality and aging in the sleep heart health study
claims.supporting_quote: Older age was associated with shorter sleep time, diminished sleep efficiency, and more arousals in men and women.

claims.claim: A systematic review of 71 studies found worse sleep in pathological aging than in healthy older adults, with REM sleep, efficiency, latency, and duration commonly compromised in Alzheimer’s disease and mild cognitive impairment.
claims.episode_span: A 2022 systematic review in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health pooled 71 studies.
claims.source_title: Sleep Quality and Aging: A Systematic Review on Healthy Older People, Mild Cognitive Impairment and Alzheimer's Disease
claims.supporting_quote: A total of 71 studies were included, and the whole sample had a mean age that ranged from 58.3 to 93.7 years

claims.claim: In the Metropolit 1953 Danish Male Birth Cohort, processing speed declined over ten years and baseline sleep microstructure correlated with cognitive outcomes in exploratory analyses.
claims.episode_span: Over ten years, Trail Making Test B slowed by 6.1 seconds and the Symbol Digit Modalities Test fell by 2.3 points.
claims.source_title: Sleep microstructure and cognitive trajectories in healthy aging
claims.supporting_quote: Over ten years, processing speed (TMT-B: +6.1 s) and symbol conversion (SDMT: -2.3) declined significantly.

claims.claim: In 24 older adults, higher REM sleep EEG slowing was associated with cortical cholinergic denervation measured by FEOBV-PET.
claims.episode_span: Higher rapid-eye-movement EEG slowing, the ratio of slower to faster power, over frontal, central, parietal, occipital, and temporal derivations was associated with cortical cholinergic denervation
claims.source_title: Associations between REM sleep EEG slowing and brain cholinergic denervation in aging and Mild Cognitive Impairment
claims.supporting_quote: Higher REM sleep EEG slowing over frontal (F3-F4), central (C3-C4), parietal (P3-P4), occipital (O1-O2) and temporal (T5-T6) derivations was significantly associated with cortical cholinergic denervation

claims.claim: A 2015 review describes reduced slow-wave sleep, spindles, and REM density with healthy aging, preserved declarative sleep-dependent consolidation, and further sleep loss in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer’s disease.
claims.episode_span: With healthy aging, a 2015 review in Current Topics in Behavioral Neurosciences describes less slow-wave sleep and less of its spectral power, fewer and smaller spindles, lower rapid-eye-movement density
claims.source_title: Sleep-dependent memory consolidation in healthy aging and mild cognitive impairment
claims.supporting_quote: Changes include reductions in slow-wave sleep's (SWS) percent and spectral power in the sleep electroencephalogram (EEG), number and amplitude of sleep spindles, rapid eye movement (REM) density and the amplitude of circadian rhythms, as well as a phase advance

claims.claim: A 2018 review proposes low-grade inflammation as a mediator among impaired sleep, dysfunctional adiposity, and cognitive decline, without new cohort data.
claims.episode_span: A 2018 review in Sleep Medicine Reviews proposes that chronic low-grade inflammation, called inflammaging, may mediate links among impaired sleep, dysfunctional adiposity, and cognitive decline
claims.source_title: Low-grade inflammation in the relationship between sleep disruption, dysfunctional adiposity, and cognitive decline in aging
claims.supporting_quote: we discuss here evidence supporting the potential mediating role of chronic low-grade systemic inflammation in the complex relationship between impaired sleep, dysfunctional adiposity, and cognitive decline through the common pathway of neuroinflammation.
